implementerProof.how: Review round 4's four findings and its one report are each answered by a claim I drove rather than read. (1) The second-order rule's terms are now nine named variables, and every one of them resolves onto the issue's volume in this live role container: XDG_CACHE_HOME=/legion/scratch/cache, XDG_DATA_HOME=/legion/scratch/data, XDG_STATE_HOME=/legion/scratch/state/tester, TMPDIR=/legion/scratch/tmp, GOCACHE=/legion/go/build, GOMODCACHE=/legion/go/mod, BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/legion/scratch/bun/install/cache, UV_CACHE_DIR=/legion/uv/cache, UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/legion/uv/python/infra-221 — with df showing /legion as the 49 GiB issue volume at 5.2 GiB used, the figure the page now gives. The excluded one is excluded for the stated reason: XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/home/legion/.config, which /proc/mounts shows as a tmpfs and manifest.go builds as an EmptyDir of StorageMediumMemory (configVolume, manifest.go:542) mounted into every role container (:459) — the page's 'the pod's shared in-memory volume', which is manifest.go:725's own phrase. (2) The cost sentence, both halves measured: df puts /home/legion on the container root (`none 8.0E /`) and the pod spec mounts no volume there (this pod's tester container mounts issue at /legion and at the sessions subpath, config at /home/legion/.config, and nothing at $HOME), so an install under $HOME is per role, per pod and gone on relaunch, while the nine paths are on the issue's 9p volume shared by the issue's roles. (3) The five sites of an image change, tested by adding a sixth: in a scratch copy of packages/daemon I added `tree` at the four Go sites (image.go's onPath list, capabilities.go's row Summary, capabilitiestest.go's `binaries`, image_test.go's expected detail) and `go test ./internal/capabilities/...` stayed green; dropping the stub-binaries site alone turned four tests red ('capability toolchain is missing: tree is not on PATH'), dropping the Summary site alone turned TestToolchainSummaryNamesTheListToolchainChecks red, and dropping the expected-detail site alone turned TestCheckImageRendersEveryRowWhenEveryImageRowIsPresent red — so the list is neither short nor padded, and the page's 'a pull request that stops at the first two opens red' is literally true. (4) `dig -v` in a pod of this round's image: `dig -v 2>/dev/null` prints `DiG 9.20.30-1~deb13u1-Debian` and `dig -v 2>&1 >/dev/null` prints nothing — stdout, as the corrected comment says. (5) sqlite3's new reason is true of this container: the session is results.jsonl, state.json and title under XDG_STATE_HOME with no .db anywhere under it, and ~/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/ holds agent.db, models.db and history.db; the same correction is in all four copies (Dockerfile:496-499, image.go:255-257, tools.md:20-23 and the bundle's copy). (6) The opening clause no longer claims the five are on PATH now, and the measurement behind that is this container: `command -v psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig` exits 1 with nothing on the digest the deployment pins today. (7) The record check: implement.json's trickyParts records that the second-order case was ruled by the architect on 2026-10-24 rather than left unsettled, and what the ruling was.

proof.criterion: The choice is written down with the measurement that decided it — the second-order rule's terms and its cost sentence, both of which name things a role can measure.
proof.surface: This live role container's environment, mounts and df, and its own pod object read from the cluster.
proof.command: printenv for each of the nine named variables and XDG_CONFIG_HOME; df -h /legion /home/legion "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME" /; grep /legion and tmpfs in /proc/mounts; kubectl -n legion get pod legion-infra-infra-221 -o json, reading the tester container's volumeMounts and resources
proof.observed: All nine resolve under /legion: /legion/scratch/{cache,data,state/tester,tmp,bun/install/cache}, /legion/go/{build,mod}, /legion/uv/cache and /legion/uv/python/infra-221. df: /legion is 49G with 5.2G used on a 9p mount (the issue volume, and the page's own figures); / is the container root; /home/legion/.config is a 16G tmpfs. XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/home/legion/.config is therefore the in-memory one the page excludes, and the code agrees — configVolume is an EmptyDir with Medium: Memory (manifest.go:542) mounted at xdgConfigHome in every role container (manifest.go:459), described there (manifest.go:725) in the words the page uses. The pod object shows the tester container mounting issue at /legion and at /home/legion/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/sessions, config at /home/legion/.config, and no volume at $HOME, so $HOME is the container's own filesystem: per role, per pod, lost on relaunch, which is the page's second half.
proof.negativeControl: The previous head's text is the control and is what review round 4 failed: it sanctioned an install under `$HOME` while also requiring the write to land on the issue's volume, and df shows those are different filesystems (`none 8.0E /` against `none 49G /legion`). The excluded variable is the second control: writing under XDG_CONFIG_HOME would satisfy 'a variable the runtime sets' and still be lost with the pod, since that path is an in-memory EmptyDir — which is why the page names it as the exclusion rather than leaving the reader to infer the list.

proof.criterion: A tool no runner reaches is an image change a worker can actually carry out — the five sites, tested by adding a sixth tool rather than by reading the list.
proof.surface: A scratch copy of packages/daemon outside the workspace (with packages/contracts/fixtures beside it, which its tests read), running the repository's own Go tests.
proof.command: cp -r packages/daemon and packages/contracts/fixtures to /tmp/probe; go test ./internal/capabilities/... as a baseline; add `tree` at the four Go sites the page names (image.go's onPath list, capabilities.go's Toolchain Summary, capabilitiestest.go's binaries, image_test.go's expected detail) and run it again; then revert one site at a time and run it again each time
proof.observed: Baseline green (ok, 38.1 s). With `tree` at all four Go sites: still green (ok, 38.4 s) — so the list is sufficient for the Go half, and nothing outside those files had to change. Reverting the stub-binaries site alone: four tests red, each naming the tool — TestReportRendersEveryRowInTableOrder, TestCheckImageRendersEveryRowWhenEveryImageRowIsPresent, TestCheckImageNamesEveryMissingRow and TestCheckImageNamesTheOneBinaryOffPATH, with 'capability toolchain is missing: tree is not on PATH'. Reverting the Summary site alone: TestToolchainSummaryNamesTheListToolchainChecks red, printing both strings. Reverting the expected-detail site alone: TestCheckImageRendersEveryRowWhenEveryImageRowIsPresent red on the detail. So each of the four Go sites is load-bearing, and with the apt line that is five files, as both AGENTS.md and the reference now say. A grep for the list's last members across the tree finds no sixth enumeration outside those files and the documentation copies.
proof.negativeControl: Three, each a site dropped and the suite run again, above: the page's claim that 'a pull request that stops at the first two opens red' is the case it describes, and I drove the two sites it was previously silent about to red individually rather than together. The scratch copy was deleted afterwards and the workspace was never modified.

proof.criterion: What the documents say about the image is true of the image — this round's dig stream, the sqlite3 reason, and the opening clause's boundary.
proof.surface: A Job in this role's own cluster namespace (its name read from the projected token file) on the image this round's code published, ghcr.io/sjawhar/legion-worker:sha-c2881a4202ff — which is this head's image content, the only later commit (a03027b2) changing Dockerfile comments and docs alone — plus this live role container on the digest the deployment pins today.
proof.command: In the Job: dig -v 2>/dev/null; dig -v 2>&1 >/dev/null; command -v psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig; ls -l /home/legion/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/; grep the round's rewrite in the image's own copy of the reference; legion probe-image --plugin-root /opt/legion/pi-legion --envoy-plugin-root /opt/legion/pi-envoy --skip-agent-models. In this container: command -v for the five; ls of $XDG_STATE_HOME/dispatch/sessions/<id>/ and find for *.db; ls of the profile databases.
proof.observed: dig: `dig -v 2>/dev/null` printed `DiG 9.20.30-1~deb13u1-Debian` and `dig -v 2>&1 >/dev/null` printed nothing — stdout, so the corrected comment is right and the previous 'on stderr' was not. The five resolve at /usr/bin/{psql,redis-cli,sqlite3,nc,dig} in that image and `legion probe-image` printed the 16-name toolchain row and 'probe-image: OK … daemon-api-version=35'. sqlite3's new reason holds in both places: the image's /home/legion/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/ carries agent.db and models.db (with its -shm and -wal), and in this container that directory also holds history.db, while the session at $XDG_STATE_HOME/dispatch/sessions/<id>/ is exactly results.jsonl, state.json and title with no .db found anywhere beneath it. The opening clause's boundary is measured here: on the digest the deployment pins today `command -v psql redis-cli sqlite3 nc dig` prints nothing and exits 1, which is the case the new wording covers ('a role still on an older digest finds none of them') and the old wording ('each of these is on your PATH now') did not.
proof.negativeControl: The two streams are each other's control for dig (redirect stderr away and the line survives; redirect stdout away and nothing is left), and today's pinned digest is the control for the opening clause — the five are absent in the container reading the sentence, which is the reason the sentence had to change. The two gates driven to failure in earlier rounds still stand: a dummy `nc` first on PATH fails the build step's assertion, and `psql` removed from a reconstructed PATH fails the capability row by name.

ciRead: At the code head a03027b2d2b50239b2800e2f99728206c96d8169, read as check runs: lint, typecheck and pr-title success with test still in progress — of the four the base requires, three are green and one is running — and build, changes, claude-envoy, envoy-plugin, pi-envoy, pi-legion and pi-shared success, the rest skipped. The handoff head 2f39167daf3af073a638b8fb2677181e35a00ae3 carries zero check runs and its commit ends `skip-checks: true`, right for a `.legion/`-only push. observations: Two precision notes for the reviewer, neither a failure, both measured. First: 'charged to the gigabyte of ephemeral storage the container is admitted with' is the repository's own established idiom (names.go:45, manifest.go:706 and :753, version.go:283, manifest_test.go:645), and the live figures are per role rather than one gigabyte — in this pod, 512Mi for the architect, planner and merger, 1536Mi for the reviewer, 3Gi for the tester and 4Gi for the implementer. The sentence's point (an install under $HOME is charged to a small per-container allowance rather than to the issue's volume) is exactly right; the number is the house idiom, not this deployment's.

Second: 'Under one of those variables it is on the issue's volume: it outlives the pod, every role of the issue shares it, and a later pod of the issue reuses it' is true of eight of the nine, and XDG_STATE_HOME is the exception — it is /legion/scratch/state/<role>, a directory per role, which names.go:40-42 says in as many words ('The one directory of it that is a role's own is its state home'). Everything the sanction test rests on (on the volume, outlives the pod, reused by a later pod) holds for all nine; only the sharing clause has that exception.

The fast-follow is unchanged and untouched by this round: the forms, the transcripts and the second-order paragraph are triplicated across docs/kubernetes.md, skills/legion-worker/references/tools.md and the generated bundle. Every claim I drove this round appears in each copy with the same wording, and the bundle is byte-identical to its sources.
